title: PROVE: Predict-to-Specify and Observe-to-Verify for Human-Aligned Evaluation of Mobile Manipulation
summary: Judging open-world robot manipulation is hard because layouts, articulated fixtures, and valid goal configurations vary widely. On RoboCasa365, simulator predicates agree with human judgments on only 69.09\% of rollouts, and a frontier VLM judge on 86.12\%. We present \textbf{PROVE} (Predict-to-Specify, Observe-to-Verify), which first specifies what success should look like and then checks the outcome. PROVE refines success conditions from the instruction, the initial scene, a target-object reference image, and a generated goal image. The goal image only sharpens the conditions and never serves as evidence. On 6,500 human-annotated rollouts over 65 atomic actions, PROVE reaches \textbf{96.83\%} agreement. Applied to open-source policies, it reports far lower success than native checks and changes their ranking. To reduce evaluation overhead in policy learning, we distill PROVE into \textbf{PROVE-Lite}, a 4B evaluator that needs no reference images. In one forward pass, PROVE-Lite predicts the outcome and the terminal state of each task condition. It reaches \textbf{91.20\%} agreement while running about 38$\times$ faster than PROVE. Mapped to a severity-aware reward, its diagnoses improve PPO post-training over both simulator and binary rewards.

AI.tldr: 针对开放世界移动操作成功判定与人类判断不一致的问题，PROVE 先根据指令、初始场景、目标物体参考图和生成目标图细化成功条件，再通过观测验证结果；在 RoboCasa365 的 6,500 条人工标注 rollout 上达到 96.83% 人类一致率。蒸馏出的 4B 评估器 PROVE-Lite 无需参考图，达到 91.20% 一致率且约快 38 倍，并用 severity-aware 奖励改进 PPO 后训练。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，开放世界机器人操作的成功判定很难，因为布局、铰接固定装置和有效目标配置差异很大。摘要报告 RoboCasa365 上模拟器谓词与人类判断仅在 69.09% 的 rollout 上一致，前沿 VLM 评委为 86.12%，说明现有判定与人类对齐不足。
AI.method: 输入为指令、初始场景、目标物体参考图和生成的目标图像。PROVE 先从这些信息中细化“成功应是什么样”的条件，再基于观测检查结果；生成的目标图像只用于锐化条件，不作为证据。相对原生检查，它改变成功判定并用于评估开源策略。PROVE-Lite 将 PROVE 蒸馏为 4B 评估器，不需参考图，在一次前向中预测每个任务条件的结果和终态；其诊断映射为 severity-aware 奖励用于 PPO 后训练。

AI.conclusion: 若这些作者报告成立，PROVE 把移动操作评估从模拟器谓词转向“先规定成功条件、再观测验证”，可提高与人类判断的一致性，并可能改变策略排名和训练奖励信号；PROVE-Lite 显示用 4B 蒸馏评估器降低评估开销的路径。证据仅来自摘要，未报告真实机器人验证，PPO 改进只有定性方向，不能推断更大范围泛化或部署效果。

title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
comment: Project page: this https URL Code: this https URL Data: this https URL
summary: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. Even with arms attached, DexEngine tracks objects more accurately than prior floating-hand methods and runs over 10x faster than RL-based ones. Policies trained on our data far outperform those trained on the same clips without physics correction or with the arms attached after a floating-hand correction, showing that fine-tuning data need physics correction. Mid-training on our data further improves them at equal fine-tuning budget, in simulation and on a real robot.

AI.tldr: 针对人→机械手重定向动作难以直接训练整机策略的问题，DexEngine 提出一条仿真流水线：先让机械臂够到手物运动，再生成跟手的手臂动作，最后用残差强化学习在物理仿真中修正，从而把人类手物数据扩成可直接训练的臂-手轨迹。作者称即使接上手臂，其物体跟踪精度仍优于先前的浮动手方法，且比基于 RL 的方法快 10 倍以上。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，已有工作多聚焦于把人类手物演示重定向到机械手；但要训练整机（whole-robot）策略，重定向后的动作必须同时满足运动学可行、物理可执行，并且要能规模化高效产出——这三点是当前重定向数据未同时满足的缺口。
AI.method: 输入是九个人类手物数据集中的手物运动片段；DexEngine 先在机械臂可达范围内放置每个片段的手物运动，再求解一条跟随人手运动的手臂轨迹，然后用残差强化学习在物理仿真中对该运动做修正，输出可直接用于训练的、物理可执行的臂-手轨迹数据。相对基线（浮动手重定向方法、纯 RL 方法），改变的是"接上手臂"与"物理修正"这两个环节及其生成效率。
AI.result: 作者报告三类结果：数据规模上，从九个数据集为四种灵巧手各生成约 5,200 个片段，并扩增为 65,000 条轨迹（116 小时）与 325,000 个 episode（578 小时）；效率与精度上，称接上手臂后其物体跟踪精度仍优于先前的浮动手方法，且比基于 RL 的方法快 10 倍以上（摘要未给出具体精度数值与单位）；策略训练上，称用其数据训练的策略远超"同一批片段但无物理修正"或"浮动手修正后再接手臂"训练的策略，并称在相同微调预算下用其数据做 mid-training 可进一步提升，且结果覆盖仿真与真机。以上均为作者自述，未经独立验证。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能数据与仿真方向，该工作把"人手物演示→整机可执行数据"的流水线作为数据放大手段，并主张物理修正对微调数据是必要的、其数据可同时用于仿真与真机策略。证据边界：摘要未给出精度指标数值、基线具体名称、真机平台、任务与样本量，也未报告消融细节或统计显著性，因此只能视作作者自述的结论。

title: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
summary: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. In contrast, holes covering about one-sixth of the wrist image eliminate the detectable benefit of depth. The validity mask strongly influences depth reliance: marking a small fraction of pixels as invalid reduces reliance, while filling holes and marking them valid restores most of the benefit. Policies trained on clean depth also lose performance when holes appear only at deployment, sometimes falling below RGB-only performance. These findings suggest that depth cameras for learned policies should therefore be judged by depth coverage more than measurement precision.

AI.tldr: 用真实腕部双目相机标定传感器模型，在仿真中分离评估深度噪声与空洞对 RGB-D 模仿策略的影响；完整深度约提升十个百分点成功率，而约六分之一腕部图像的空洞即可抹去该收益，说明深度覆盖率比测量精度更关键。
AI.motivation: 一些研究报告传感器深度带来收益，另一些却因测量噪声而回避深度相机；深度图中的噪声与缺失值（空洞）各自造成多大影响此前并不清楚。
AI.method: 输入是 RGB 图像与深度图（含噪声/空洞以及有效性掩码），输出是不同条件下的策略成功率与失败模式归因。先用真实腕部双目相机标定出一个传感器模型，再在仿真中把噪声与空洞分别注入到 RGB-D 模仿策略的观测中，用三种视觉编码器比较成功率；并额外考察有效性掩码的标注方式、空洞填补，以及仅在部署阶段才出现空洞（策略在干净深度上训练）的情形。相对基线的变化在于把“深度噪声”与“深度空洞”作为两个可独立控制的变量来评估，而不是笼统地比较“有无深度”。
AI.result: 作者报告：完整深度使成功率提升约十个百分点，且该收益在相机噪声水平二十倍时大部分仍然保留；相比之下，覆盖约六分之一腕部图像的空洞会消除可检测到的深度收益。有效性掩码强烈影响对深度的依赖：把少量像素标为无效会降低依赖，填补空洞并标为有效则可恢复大部分收益。此外，仅在部署时出现空洞会使在干净深度上训练的策略性能下降，有时甚至低于仅用 RGB 的表现。摘要未报告绝对成功率数值、具体任务或基准名称、统计显著性与真实机器人策略结果；作者据此主张深度相机应按覆盖率而非测量精度来评判（属作者结论，未经独立验证）。
AI.conclusion: 对学习型操作策略而言，深度相机的价值主要由深度覆盖率决定，而非测量精度。证据边界：真实双目相机只用于标定传感器模型，策略评估在仿真中进行，摘要未给出真实机器人部署结果、三个视觉编码器名称与量化基线。

title: $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM: Efficient Hierarchical Memory Across Modalities and Timescales for World-Action Models
summary: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. Within the same short- and long-term hierarchy, interaction memory encodes executed action prefixes into compact temporal representations, complementing visual observations with behavioral context. These complementary memories are integrated into world-action modeling through layer-wise retrieval, enabling memory-augmented action generation with a bounded online memory footprint independent of episode length. On the memory-dependent simulation benchmarks MIKASA-Robo and RMBench, $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves +53.2% and +61.2% absolute improvements in average success rates over Fast-WAM, respectively. These gains extend to real-world manipulation, where $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM achieves a +29.3% absolute improvement over LingBot-VA in average success across three tasks. These results suggest that $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM offers a promising approach to efficient memory-augmented world-action modeling.

AI.tldr: 针对长程操作中视觉历史存储开销大、压缩又易丢失细节的问题，M²-WAM 用视觉短/长期记忆与动作交互记忆的分层机制，在固定在线内存下生成动作。作者报告其在两个仿真基准和三项真实任务上提升平均成功率。
AI.motivation: 长程机器人操作依赖历史上下文；保留大量视觉历史会带来持续增长的存储与检索成本，而激进压缩可能丢掉后续决策所需的细粒度信息。已执行动作历史还包含稀疏视觉观测可能遗漏的中间行为，因此需要按模态区分的记忆机制来平衡近期细节与长期保留。
AI.method: 输入为近期视觉观测与已执行动作前缀。模型将近期视觉观测保存在稠密短期记忆中，把被挤出窗口的条目通过门控 delta 更新写入固定大小的关联长期记忆；交互记忆在同一短/长期层级内把动作前缀编码为紧凑时序表示。两类记忆经逐层检索注入世界-动作建模，输出记忆增强的动作，并使在线内存占用不随回合长度增长。
AI.result: 作者报告：在 MIKASA-Robo 与 RMBench 上，平均成功率较 Fast-WAM 分别绝对提升 +53.2% 与 +61.2%；在三项真实世界操作任务上，平均成功率较 LingBot-VA 绝对提升 +29.3%。摘要未报告误差、样本量或统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 该工作表明，按模态与时间尺度分离记忆、并用固定大小长期记忆控制开销，是长程世界-动作建模的一条可行路径。证据限于作者报告的模拟基准与三项真实任务的平均成功率，尚不足以判断各记忆组件的单独贡献或更广泛部署效果。

title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, to be presented at 1st Workshop on Physical World AI at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Recent test-time steering methods have shown promise in enabling adaptive VLA policies by utilizing additional computation during deployment. In this paper, we consider best-of-$N$ test-time steering for VLA models, where multiple action candidates are sampled from a fixed policy and a verifier is used to select the best one during deployment. We show that increasing $N$ does not always improve performance when the verifier is inaccurate, and can favor candidates whose scores exploit prediction errors, a form of reward hacking. We study this effect on 60 LIBERO-Safety task-level cases using a $\pi_{0.5}$ policy, with ten repetitions per case. We introduce controlled errors in a MuJoCo trajectory verifier and show that as $N$ increases, selected candidate rewards diverge from the accurate verifier rewards, leading to reward hacking. We also show that verifier calibration and softmax-based candidate selection can mitigate reward hacking in some settings.

title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
summary: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. Each candidate action induces a sparse object-factor causal graph describing the physical pathways it activates. Rolling out these graphs under the shared situation anchors predictions to observed outcomes and confines action contrasts to the objects each action reaches. Shared type-conditioned functions support varying numbers of objects, while a round-trip loss enforces action-invariant abduction without counterfactual labels. We show that replacing an individual effect with its conditional mean incurs mean-squared error equal to its conditional variance, motivating comparisons between coupled futures. Building on these comparisons, Counterfactual Advantage Planning (CAP) ranks plans by their advantage over an incumbent within shared situations and constrains the probability of harm. Paired advantages reduce estimator variance by a factor of $1-\rho$, where $\rho$ is the correlation between branch outcomes, and cancel model errors shared by both branches. Each executed transition provides hindsight advantages to update the physics posterior, the next plan, and an amortized policy without a learned critic. We further establish when observational transitions identify interventional dynamics. Paired simulator interventions evaluate counterfactual accuracy, graph recovery, compositional generalization, and decision quality.

AI.tldr: 只用事实转移无法比较同一情境下不同动作的个体效应。WhatIf 用共享潜物理与动作诱导的稀疏物体因子因果图耦合候选未来，并以反事实优势规划排序计划、约束伤害概率；摘要只给出理论结论与仿真评估任务清单，未报告数值结果。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：世界模型能预测某个动作之后会发生什么，但要在同一物理情境中比较多个动作，仅靠事实转移只能得到各动作的边际未来与平均效应，得不到个体效应，也得不到"换成另一个动作会造成伤害"的概率。
AI.method: 输入是已执行转移构成的事实历史、当前观测到的情境，以及一组候选动作。方法把候选未来绑定到同一份从事实历史推断出的潜物理与转移噪声上，使它们在同一情境中"耦合"；每个候选动作诱导一张稀疏的物体因子因果图，描述该动作激活的物理通路，展开这些图时以观测结果锚定预测，并把动作之间的对比限制在该动作实际触及的物体上。共享的类型条件函数支持物体数量变化，往返损失（round-trip loss）在没有反事实标签的情况下实现动作不变的溯因。在此之上，反事实优势规划（CAP）用相对现任计划的优势值排序，并约束伤害概率；每次实际执行的转移提供事后（hindsight）优势，用于更新物理后验、下一个计划和一个摊薄策略，无需学习 critic。相对仅建模事实转移/平均效应的基线，改变的是"把候选未来耦合起来比较个体效应"。

title: Keep or Roll Back? Out-of-Loop Judges for Self-Improving VLA and End-to-End Embodied Policies
summary: Self-improvement is now a practical recipe for embodied policies: a policy collects experience, is retrained, and is kept when a judge rates it higher. However, the judge is usually trained or chosen inside the same loop, so its evidence is not independent of the policy. We introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that adds a sealed judge: an evaluator outside the loop that the improver cannot see or optimize against. A new policy is kept only when a sequential test on the sealed judge confirms the gain, with a bounded probability of keeping a worse one. Running the same loop under each judge, we separate two sources of a false gain, which we call judge error (the loop's judge is wrong on its own data) and transfer gap (a real gain there does not carry over to unseen conditions). We evaluate on LIBERO manipulation, NAVSIM driving, and a full-scale real vehicle. In manipulation, a success classifier accepted 65 of 196 failures in one generation. In driving, policies that gain on the loop's own frames lose in an unseen city, so even an exact in-loop judge would keep 8/15 of them. When the sealed test decides, a driving loop built to improve ends with a better policy than under its own critic (0.674 against 0.649 PDMS, from 0.638), and on driving pairs with known sealed gain the test accepted 11 of 12 real gains and none of 59 losses. In a real-world field experiment on a published improvement step, the reinforced version drove further into a curve than the version it started from in all 6 blind pairs, though neither completed it. These results show that evidence from inside the loop, however accurate, is not enough to decide whether a policy has improved. SealedLoop offers a foundation for trustworthy self-improvement of embodied policies, in which progress is judged by evidence the improving system cannot influence.

AI.tldr: 自改进闭环通常由与策略同源的评判者决定"保留还是回滚"，其证据并不独立；SealedLoop 用闭环外、改进者看不到也无法优化 的密封评判者做序贯检验来下保留决定。作者在 LIBERO、NAVSIM 与实车实验中报告，闭环内证据即使准确也会保留假增益，而密封检验接受了 11/12 的真实增益、0/59 的损失。
AI.motivation: 自改进已成为具身策略的实用做法：策略收集经验、被重训，并在评判者给出更高评分时被保留。但评判者通常在同一闭环内训练或选择，其证据与策略不独立，因此无法回答"策略是否真的变好"这一问题。
AI.method: 输入是常规的自改进闭环：策略收集经验、重训，再由评判者打分为新版本决定保留或回滚。SealedLoop 在此之上加入一个"密封评判者"——位于闭环之外、改进者看不到也无法对其优化的评估器；只有当密封评判者上的序贯检验确认增益时，新策略才被保留，且保留一个更差策略的概率有界。该设置把假增益拆成两类：评判误差（闭环评判者在自己数据上判断错误）与迁移差距（在那里真实的增益无法迁移到未见条件）。输出是每个候选检查点的保留/回滚决策，以及两类失败来源的分解，并在 LIBERO 操作、NAVSIM 驾驶和一辆全尺度实车上评估。
AI.result: 在 LIBERO 操作中，闭环内的成功分类器在一代之内把 196 次失败中的 65 次判为成功（评判误差）。在 NAVSIM 驾驶中，在闭环自有帧上获得增益的策略在未见城市中变差，作者称即使使用完全精确的闭环评判者也会保留其中 8/15（迁移差距）。当由密封检验决定时，一个以改进为目标的驾驶闭环得到的策略优于使用其自身 critic 的结果：0.674 对 0.649 PDMS，起点为 0.638；在已知密封增益的驾驶配对上，检验接受了 12 个真实增益中的 11 个，59 个损失中一个也未接受。在真实车辆现场实验中，针对一个已发表的改进步骤，强化版本在全部 6 组盲配对中都比其起点版本沿弯道行驶得更远，但两者都未完成该弯道。摘要未报告种子数、重复次数与统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身策略的自改进而言，结论是：来自闭环内部的证据无论多准确，都不足以判断策略是否真正改进，保留/回滚决定需要由改进者无法影响的证据来做出。该结论由作者自报，未经独立验证；证据边界限于摘要，密封评判者的构造方式、序贯检验的具体统计保证与阈值均未在摘要中给出，因此不能推断其在其他机器人形态或任务上的普适性。

title: Fast Muscle-Driven Whole-Body Motion Tracking with a Differentiable World Model
summary: Tracking motion capture with a whole-body musculoskeletal model means coordinating hundreds of muscles through contact, and current controllers take hours to days of GPU time to train, so every tuning decision is expensive. SuperMimic trains a tracking policy by backpropagating through the rollouts of a learned world model. We extend it to MS-Human-700 (700 muscles) and MyoFullBody (354 muscles), with MuJoCo's activation dynamics inside the world model. To make its training fast, our recipe takes the speedups developed for the Unitree G1, replaces three of their settings that fail on muscles, and adds four changes of our own: observations without muscle geometry, data collection concurrent with the updates, Beta exploration noise that keeps every excitation in $[0,1]$, and 50 Hz control. On one RTX 5090 it trains MS-Human-700 in 6.3 minutes to the held-out return that SuperMimic's published hyperparameters reach in 3.9 hours, 37$\times$ sooner, and in 20 minutes to lower tracking errors than theirs after 10 hours. It trains MyoFullBody 34$\times$ sooner without retuning. Ablations show what is specific to muscles: a higher policy learning rate stalls half of the runs, and clipped Gaussian noise adds a tonic co-contraction that Beta noise avoids. Finally, refining the policy's actions through the world model at test time lowers the position error by a further 26% with no held-out clip failing, and reaches the same return after 5.1 instead of 6.3 minutes of training. title: Integration of Vision-Language-Action Control for Autonomous Forklift Unloading with Limited Real-World Data
summary: Forklifts play a critical role in warehousing and distribution, but existing automation systems remain limited in handling complex tasks that require sequential decision-making. Recently, vision--language--action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising approach for multi-step decision-making by directly generating control actions from visual observations and language prompts. Although VLA-based control has been extensively researched for manipulators, to the best of our knowledge, its application to forklifts remains unexplored. Therefore, this study demonstrates the integration of VLA control for an autonomous forklift unloading task with limited real-world data. Moreover, training VLA models typically requires large-scale datasets. As there is currently no public dataset for forklift operations, we use a VLA model pretrained primarily on robotic manipulator data and construct a training dataset via simulation, which can be scaled up at low cost. We then adapt the pretrained VLA model to forklift control using 9.38 h of simulation data and 0.8 h of real-world demonstrations, with the latter accounting for approximately 8% of the collected forklift data by duration. The integrated system was validated through 72 real-world trials across four model variants. The results show that the proposed system can accomplish an unloading task even with limited real-world data.

AI.method: 输入是视觉观测与语言提示，输出是直接生成的控制动作。做法是：先取一个主要在机械臂数据上预训练的 VLA 模型，再通过仿真构建可低成本扩展的叉车训练数据集，最后用 9.38 h 仿真数据和 0.8 h 真机演示（按时长约占所收集叉车数据的 8%）把预训练模型适配到叉车控制。相对基线的变化在于把原本面向机械臂的 VLA 控制迁移到叉车卸货，而非另建专用自动化流水线。

title: Learning a Whole-Body Pivot-Walking Gait for Heavy-Box Transport with a Humanoid
comment: Accepted to IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026. 8 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Project page: this https URL Video: this https URL
summary: Through pivot walking, humans can transport objects that are too heavy to lift. Previous humanoid studies have relied on planned sequences in which object manipulation and stepping are executed separately and the object is brought to rest between successive rotations. However, few studies have developed a single learned controller for humanoid pivot walking. In this paper, we propose a single reinforcement-learning policy that jointly coordinates stepping, balance control, and object manipulation. The policy is trained using rewards that promote alternating pivot motions and a phase reference that progresses according to the displacement of the object. In simulation, we confirmed that the humanoid can pivot a box. For deployment, we fine-tuned the policy into an object-blind version that follows a periodic clock instead of the progress reference. On the real robot, the deployed policy transported the box forward by more than 1 m in all five trials; each trial ended at a base-tilt safety stop. These results demonstrate that coordinated humanoid pivot walking can be learned with reinforcement learning and transferred to a physical humanoid robot without direct object-state sensing.

title: iMFPO: Improving Mean Flow Policy Optimization with Drift-Aware Velocity Alignment for Embodied Control
summary: Flow-based generative policies offer expressive action modeling for embodied control, yet achieving efficient one-step generation under reward-driven policy optimization remains challenging. In particular, evolving action distributions during online reinforcement learning may introduce inconsistencies between instantaneous-velocity learning and interval-averaged action generation. To address this challenge, we propose iMFPO, a one-step generative policy optimization framework with decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment. A shared interval-conditioned actor supports instantaneous-velocity supervision and interval-averaged action generation. JVP-corrected velocity regression is jointly optimized with reward-driven policy objectives, with action-level guidance from a frozen PPO teacher during training. At inference, iMFPO directly generates actions through interval-averaged velocity prediction, achieving one-step control without iterative flow integration. Across Go2, G1, H1, and Spot, zero-latent evaluation yields mean returns of 35.69, 34.44, 416.23, and 29.86. On Go2, action-generation latency drops from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms relative to 64-step RFPO. title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
summary: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. this https URL

AI.tldr: SEEK 让机器人把跨尝试的执行知识留存下来：用可执行程序式策略表示"怎么做"，用动作-效果库记录"做出来是什么效果"，底层多模态模型保持不变。在 RoboDojo 上作者报告十次尝试后平均任务分从 27.0 升至 54.4、成功率从 19.7% 升至 48.0%。
AI.motivation: 通用多模态基础模型能让机器人在部署时依靠观测与执行反馈适应任务，但学习成果只留在模型的工作上下文里，任务结束后就丢失这类执行知识（例如如何在两个夹爪之间搬运一个碗），下次尝试可能同样慢、重复同样的错误。作者指出两条既有路线的不足：重放过去的动作不够，因为动作效果取决于当前条件；而按当前场景决定动作的程序式做法，一旦遇到此前尝试未覆盖的条件，修订就需要早先动作的实测效果。
AI.method: 输入是当前场景观测与执行反馈，以及此前尝试累积的留存知识。SEEK 同时保留两类知识：Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy（SEPP）把操作写成可执行程序，并依据当前观测决定每一步动作；机器人执行过程中，SEEK 把动作的实测效果（包括失败尝试产生的效果）写入 Persistent Action-Effect Bank（PAEB）。输出是行动：当已留存程序适用时直接动作、不请求模型；当遇到程序未覆盖的条件时，则以 PAEB 中的实测证据为依据修订程序。相对直接调用基础模型的基线，改变在于把知识从易失的工作上下文搬到可跨尝试持久化并自我修订的程序与效果记录中，而底层模型权重保持不变。
AI.result: 作者报告在 RoboDojo 全部 42 个任务上，保留十次尝试的知识使 SEEK 的平均任务分从 27.0 提升到 54.4，成功率从 19.7% 提升到 48.0%。在其中的 34 个任务上，使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 时 SEEK 五次尝试后达到 80.1，同一模型直接执行时为 49.6，且模型请求量减少 77.6%。摘要未说明 27.0 与 80.1 的度量口径、单位，也未说明 RoboDojo 属于仿真还是真实机器人评测。

title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Cross-Embodiment Robot Control
summary: Language-instructed manipulation requires robust closedloop policies, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are costly and limited in coverage. Human and robot videos provide complementary spatiotemporal priors for crossembodiment control. We propose X-World, which adapts pretrained video diffusion to variable views. A Q-Former compresses hidden states into tokens for a shared flowmatching expert that predicts action chunks. Datasetspecific projections map native states and actions. We adapt the backbone on large-scale robot and human videos, freeze it for action-only pretraining of the Q-Former and action expert, then post-train on the target platform. At inference, X-World responds at 20 Hz and overlaps updates with execution via asynchronous real-time chunking. X-World performs strongly on LIBERO and under zero-shot shifts on LIBERO-Plus. On hardware, it averages 81.7% success across six bimanual tasks on the side-mounted dual-arm UR5e, one of three real-robot configurations presented.

AI.tldr: 动作标注机器人轨迹昂贵且覆盖有限，X-World 把预训练视频扩散适配到可变视角，用 Q-Former 压缩隐状态并由共享 flow-matching 专家预测动作块。摘要称其在 LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus 表现强，真机侧装双臂 UR5e 六任务平均成功率为 81.7%，推理响应 20 Hz。
AI.motivation: 语言指令操作需要鲁棒的闭环策略，但动作标注机器人轨迹成本高、覆盖有限。人类视频与机器人视频可提供互补的时空先验，问题在于如何把这类视频先验用于跨本体控制。
AI.method: 输入是机器人与人类视频（用于适配预训练视频扩散骨干）、可变视角，以及各本体的原生状态与动作。Q-Former 把隐状态压缩为 token，交给共享的 flow-matching 专家预测动作块；数据集特定投影将原生状态和动作映射到共享空间。训练上先在大规模机器人与人类视频上适配骨干，再冻结骨干、仅对 Q-Former 与动作专家做动作预训练，最后在目标平台后训练。输出是动作块，供闭环控制使用；推理时以 20 Hz 响应，并用异步实时分块把更新与执行重叠。

AI.conclusion: 该工作提示视频扩散的时空先验可通过共享专家与本体特定投影迁移到跨本体动作生成，并以异步分块支持 20 Hz 闭环。证据边界：未读全文，LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus 缺少数值、基线与条件，81.7% 仅对应三种真机配置中的一种、六个任务的平均值，不能外推到其余配置或任务。

title: Targeted Adaptation of World-Action Models via Interaction and Motion Heads
summary: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a promising new paradigm of robot manipulation policies that jointly generate future video and actions. Successful manipulation requires both identifying where to interact and modeling how the robot and objects move. Yet standard adaptation methods, such as full fine-tuning and LoRA, do not explicitly select parameters aligned with these manipulation-specific capabilities. Motivated by this challenge, we discover two functionally specialized families of attention heads: Next-Interaction Heads, which localize upcoming grasp-and-release targets, and Motion Heads, which track movement across frames. Furthermore, we introduce HeadLight, a parameter-efficient refinement method that jointly adapts Next-Interaction Heads and Motion Heads. On RoboTwin tasks unseen during fine-tuning, HeadLight achieves 62.28% success, compared with 57.89% for full fine-tuning and 58.66% for LoRA, while updating only 1.1% of parameters. Inference-time ablations further validate the functional importance of these heads: ablating Motion Heads reduces manipulation success from 57.89% to 0.94%, while ablating Next-Interaction Heads lowers it to 40.61%, both substantially more than ablating equally many random heads. Finally, we show that our approach is effective across multiple WAM architectures and real-robot manipulation settings.

AI.tldr: 世界-动作模型（WAM）需要适配以同时定位交互位置并建模运动，但全微调和 LoRA 不显式选择与这些操作能力对齐的参数。HeadLight 只联合适配 Next-Interaction Heads 与 Motion Heads，在 RoboTwin 未见任务上以 1.1% 参数更新取得 62.28% 成功率，并显示这两类头在推理时具有功能重要性。
AI.motivation: 标准适配方法（全微调、LoRA）不显式选择与操作特定能力对齐的参数；而成功操作既需要识别在哪里交互，也需要建模机器人和物体如何运动。
AI.method: 输入是联合生成未来视频和动作的 WAM 机器人操作策略。作者识别出两类功能性注意力头：Next-Interaction Heads 定位即将发生的抓取和释放目标，Motion Heads 跨帧跟踪运动。HeadLight 是一种参数高效精调方法，联合适配这两类头；相较全微调和 LoRA，关键改动是只更新与这些操作能力相关的参数（摘要报告更新 1.1% 参数）。输出是适配后的 WAM 策略，用于未见任务和真实机器人操作。
AI.result: 在 RoboTwin 微调期间未见过的任务上，HeadLight 成功率为 62.28%，全微调为 57.89%，LoRA 为 58.66%，且仅更新 1.1% 参数。推理时消融 Motion Heads 将操作成功率从 57.89% 降至 0.94%，消融 Next-Interaction Heads 降至 40.61%，均比消融同等数量随机头更严重。作者还称方法跨多种 WAM 架构和真实机器人操作设置有效，但摘要未报告对应数值。
AI.conclusion: 摘要支持的结论是：在 WAM 中显式适配功能特化的交互头与运动头，可能以极少参数更新提升未见任务的操作成功率，并且这些头对推理成功有可测量的贡献。证据边界：仅基于摘要，未提供真实机器人硬件、任务数量、统计显著性和多架构细节；不能推断超出摘要的部署或泛化能力。

title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
summary: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at this http URL .

AI.tldr: 针对动作条件世界模型在抓取错位、错时等"失败路径"上预测崩溃的问题，作者构建 62k 条扰动抓取的仿真失败轨迹，并用两种额外训练信号微调世界模型，在 Cosmos3 Nano 上把物体轨迹误差降低 28.2%。
AI.motivation: 机器人训练数据以成功演示为主，世界模型在偏离"happy path"时预测失效：摘要报告在五个预训练动作条件模型上，物体运动误差相对"复制首帧"的静态基线最多只低 10.4%，且其中两个模型还不如该静态基线。这说明现有世界模型在抓取错位、错时导致物体被推、倾斜或滑落时并不可靠。
AI.method: 输入方面，作者先用参考抓取作为种子，在位置、朝向和闭合时机上做扰动，采集 62k 条仿真轨迹构成 Reforge 数据集，每条记录对应的推挤、滑落或抓取失败，并附带真值物体位姿、接触和表面点。方法 WorldReforge 把这些真值转成两种训练信号，且不增加推理开销：Interaction Alignment 把重建损失集中到被全局损失低权重对待的小物体与接触区域；Surface Correspondence 训练主干特征在不同帧中跟踪同一物理表面点。输出是一个在失败接触下仍能预测物体运动的世界模型。
AI.result: 在 Cosmos3 Nano 上，作者报告物体轨迹误差整体降低 28.2%、未见物体上降低 35.0%，预测"两个动作结果如何分叉"的误差降低 43.3%（均为相对降幅，摘要未给出绝对数值、误差单位或基准数据集名称）。仅用仿真训练，在 DROID 和真实失败视频上重建也有改善，但摘要未给出数值。受控数据研究显示失败接触与成功抓持教给模型互补的物理规律。
AI.conclusion: 该工作把"失败"当作一种可监督信号：世界模型的短板可能不在容量，而在训练数据只覆盖成功路径与全局重建损失对小物体、接触区域的忽视。其证据边界是：主要量化结果来自仿真与单一骨干（Cosmos3 Nano），真实数据上只报告了重建改善且无数字，摘要未报告真机闭环控制、规划收益或统计显著性检验。

title: Aegis-VLA: Reliability-Gated Action Refinement via a Trajectory World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
summary: Dynamic object manipulation requires maintaining spatial and temporal alignment with targets that continue to move during inference and execution. Although future prediction can inform action correction, an accurate forecast does not establish whether modifying an existing action would be beneficial. We present Aegis-VLA, a world-model-guided vision-language-action (VLA) framework that generates predictive action corrections and separately determines whether and how strongly to apply them. A Trajectory World Model combines kinematic extrapolation with learned residual dynamics to predict object motion and estimate positional uncertainty. Discrepancy-Guided Action Refinement uses differences between history-only and base-action-conditioned end-effector forecasts to propose bounded arm corrections. A Reliability Gate learns when to admit corrections based on demonstration-relative improvements over base actions, and regulates their application during inference using predictive uncertainty and anticipated object--end-effector proximity. Rejected corrections preserve the corresponding base actions. Aegis-VLA introduces only approximately 2.45M trainable parameters. On the simulated Dynamic Object Manipulation (DOM) benchmark, Aegis-VLA achieves 56.72\% success over 1,800 evaluation trials, exceeding our reproduced DynamicVLA baseline of 45.44\% by 11.28 percentage points.

title: FailPoint-X: A Policy-Matched, Failure-Anchored Benchmark for Offline VLA Post-Training from Human Takeovers
comment: 34 pages (8-page main paper, references, and 24-page supplementary material), 9 figures, 20 tables. Zirui Li and Yujie Yan contributed equally. Project page: this https URL ; Code: this https URL
summary: Human takeovers offer corrective supervision for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, but their contribution to offline post-training must be separated from that of continued optimization. We introduce FailPoint-X, a benchmark for offline VLA post-training with human takeovers. To represent uncertainty in failure onset, an annotator marks an interval for each failure, and training takeovers start at seeded frames sampled within it. From one fixed $\pi_{0.5}$ checkpoint, which also initializes post-training, we assemble 629 natural failures across 10 LIBERO-X task families at up to five difficulty levels. All 2,823 takeover attempts are logged; 2,400 are accepted recoveries, of which 2,320 are used for post-training. Evaluation restarts every method from the fixed midpoints of 384 held-out failure intervals. Under matched actor-update counts, we compare behavior cloning of recoveries, value-based offline learning on recoveries and failed rollouts, and continued training on existing demonstrations. Within 1,200 steps on the 240 L1-L3 held-out failures, cloning improves recovery by 29.4 percentage points (pp) over the demonstration-only control; the value-based learner does not establish a further gain (1.5 pp). In exploratory evaluation from L1-L5 nominal starts at the same horizon, cloning loses 30.0 pp of success relative to the base policy; mixing in demonstrations reduces the loss to 16.5 pp, a reduction that shrinks under a stricter, pre-specified horizon. Restorable failure states and a shared evaluator let all methods be compared from identical starts.

AI.tldr: FailPoint-X 用人类接管在标注的失败区间种子帧上构建离线 VLA 后训练基准，并从同一 π0.5 checkpoint、匹配 actor 更新次数下比较方法。摘要报告：克隆在 240 个 L1–L3 held-out 失败上恢复表现较仅示范对照 +29.4 pp；但 L1–L5 nominal 起点的探索性评估中，克隆较基础策略成功率 −30.0 pp。
AI.motivation: 人类接管能提供纠正监督，但作者强调其离线后训练贡献必须与持续优化分开。失败发生时刻存在不确定性，且若更新次数或评测起点不一致，方法间收益难以归因；因此需要一个失败锚定、策略匹配且共享起点的评测。
AI.method: 输入为固定的 π0.5 checkpoint、人类接管恢复、失败 rollout 与已有示范。标注者为每次失败标出起始区间，训练接管从区间内采样的种子帧开始；接管尝试被记录并筛选为可接受恢复。所有方法由同一 checkpoint 初始化，并在匹配 actor 更新次数下比较：对恢复做行为克隆、对恢复与失败 rollout 做基于价值的离线学习、在已有示范上继续训练。输出是带可复原失败状态和共享评测器的基准；评测从 384 个 held-out 失败区间的固定中点重启，使各方法从相同起点比较。

title: SplatWAM: Splatting World Action Models for Real-Time 3D Imagination
summary: World models typically predict future observations in pixel or latent space, limiting their ability to directly represent true 3D scene evolution. We present SplatWAM (Splatting World Action Model), a generative world model that learns action-conditioned dynamics directly over compact 3D Gaussian primitives. A tokenizer SplatWAM-T first encodes a variable number of unposed views into a fixed budget of Gaussian tokens. A dynamics model SplatWAM-D then predicts future Gaussian states in a single forward pass per action, using log-Euclidean covariance coordinates and differentiable rendering supervision to facilitate learning in an explicit 3D space. Each predicted state can be rasterized from arbitrary viewpoints, enforcing a shared 3D representation across views by construction. On OGBench Scene, SplatWAM renders novel views 12x faster than video world models (~80 FPS on an RTX 5090) with up to 2.0 dB higher PSNR. We further introduce SplatWAM-P, a lightweight flow-matching policy head jointly trained with the dynamics model. Across 8 task suites, model-free Gaussian-token policies outperform pixel-based counterparts by up to 24.8 percentage points. SplatWAM-P improves over Latent Particle World Model (LPWM) by 12 percentage points and matches HIQL without a learned value function. On LIBERO, our ~1B model outperforms WorldVLA (~7B) and the robot-pretrained OpenVLA (~7B), while matching OpenVLA-OFT when both are trained without large-scale robot pretraining. Code and checkpoints will be released.

title: FreshVLA: Frequency-Regularized Time Scale Hierarchical Latent Actions for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Learning reusable latent actions from action-free videos offers an effective route to improving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. However, reconstruction-oriented latent actions do not necessarily benefit policy learning: as they may encode task-irrelevant static appearance with scene identity, or entangle slowly varying task progress with fine-grained execution dynamics in limited discrete code. We propose FreshVLA, a VLA framework built on a frequency-guided, dynamics-sensitive learning paradigm for acquiring temporally hierarchical continuous latent actions. FreshVLA uses a high-pass prior to guide visual transition encoding toward dynamical regions, thereby reducing reliance on static appearance cues. It further organizes latent actions into coarse-grained task progress and fine-grained execution dynamics through cross-timescale sampling and frequency-domain regularization, enhancing their capacity to represent long-horizon behaviors. During policy training, we freeze the pretrained latent action encoder and transfer its representations to robot control through joint flow-matching of latent and robot actions. FreshVLA achieves 98.2% average success on LIBERO and 98.0% on LIBERO-Long, exceeding GR00T-N1.6 on the latter by 3.6%. It also reaches an average sequence length of 4.52 on CALVIN and strong overall success rate of 80.4% in the zero-shot LIBERO-PLUS evaluation. Furthermore, FreshVLA exhibits greater robustness to visual perturbations and a more distinct division of roles between two branches in modeling low- and high-frequency motion, respectively. In 35-step action regression, it achieves a 51.3-percentage-point higher relative error reduction than its hierarchical discrete counterpart. Real-world experiments demonstrate that FreshVLA improves the average success rate over $\pi_{0.5}$ by 7.5%. The FreshVLA project page is available at this https URL .

title: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation
summary: Image-goal navigation asks a robot to reach the viewpoint of a target photograph without a map or goal pose. In three dimensions, this requires not only recognizing the goal but also estimating 3D displacement and generating continuous control actions to approach and settle at the target view. This is difficult because the same visual difference between current and goal image can require very different actions depending on the robot's velocity, yet monocular images alone reveal neither metric scale nor body motion. As a result, existing image-goal policies are limited to planar action spaces and rely on a state estimator for flight control. Policies that map directly from images to low-level control commands have been demonstrated for agile flight, but not toward goal images in unseen environments. We present the first image-goal navigation policy that directly commands thrust and angular rates for agile quadrotor flight in unseen 3D environments, without relying on state estimation (e.g., SLAM, VO, or SfM) or a separate velocity controller. We train a recurrent vision-based policy through a four-stage pipeline that combines geometric and motion supervision with privileged-teacher distillation and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. On 1000 held-out flights in unseen environments, the policy achieves an 82.3% success rate with a mean terminal position error of 0.10m across successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, the policy reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment.

title: WISER-RL: A Wake-Sleep Learning Mechanism for Robot Reinforcement Learning from One Demonstration
summary: A robot learning from one human demonstration may rarely succeed on its own, leaving reinforcement learning (RL) with little reward feedback. We introduce WISER-RL ({W}ake--sleep policy improvement loop, {I}mitation, and {S}elective {E}xperience {R}eplay), a composite reinforcement learning framework that turns assisted practice into autonomous control. During wake, GPTDAgger monitors disagreement among actions sampled by a diffusion policy. When disagreement crosses a threshold, a frozen GPT controller uses retrieved experience to continue the episode. During sleep, Conflict-Aware Experience Reweighting (CAER) compares visually matched successful trajectories and downweights conflicting action windows with more steps remaining to success. The policy imitates the reweighted successes and learns from both successes and failures through offline advantage-guided RL before collecting the next round. After final online PPO refinement, the autonomous policy succeeded in 100% evaluations on each of six LIBERO tasks and 100% trials on each of two real-robot tasks.

AI.tldr: 单次人类演示下策略难以自主成功、RL 缺少奖励反馈；WISER-RL 用 wake–sleep 循环（分歧触发 GPT 接管 + 冲突感知经验重加权）把辅助练习转为自主控制，最终在线 PPO 精调后在 6 个 LIBERO 任务各 100% 评测成功、2 个真机任务各 100% 试验成功。
AI.motivation: 作者指出：机器人仅凭一次人类演示学习时，很少能自主成功，导致强化学习几乎拿不到奖励反馈。
AI.method: 输入是一次人类演示，以及扩散策略采样出的动作。wake（清醒）阶段：GPTDAgger 监控扩散策略所采样动作之间的不一致程度，当不一致超过阈值时，由冻结的 GPT 控制器利用检索到的经验继续该回合。sleep（睡眠）阶段：Conflict-Aware Experience Reweighting（CAER）比较视觉上匹配的成功轨迹，对"距离成功剩余步数更多"的冲突动作窗口降权；策略模仿重加权后的成功样本，并通过离线 advantage-guided RL 同时从成功与失败中学习，然后进入下一轮收集。最后做在线 PPO 精调，输出自主策略。相对基线（单演示直接学习）的改变在于：不再只依赖稀疏奖励，而是用模型接管补足回合、再用重加权经验做模仿加离线 RL。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作提出一种把"模型接管 + 经验重加权"嵌入 RL 循环、从而在单演示条件下获得自主策略的思路，并在仿真基准与真机上均报告了 100% 成功率。但证据仅限摘要所述的这两个成功率数字：没有基线对照、没有统计信息、真机设置细节缺失，因此不能据此推断泛化能力、样本效率优势或跨任务迁移性。

title: CoTacWAM: Joint Modeling of Vision and Touch for Robotic Manipulation
summary: We present CoTacWAM, a world-action model that learns shared contact semantics between wrist vision and touch, achieving the best observed performance in our nominal manipulation and missing-input evaluations. The two modalities observe the same local interaction through different signals: wrist images reveal nearby geometry, while touch records physical contact. Our approach connects their common contact meaning while preserving the evidence unique to each modality, giving the policy a joint description of interaction across available input combinations. This representation supports predictive action learning alongside head-view scene context and conditions corrections after an independent detector confirms a failed attempt. Experiments across four real-world tasks demonstrate improved manipulation performance over the evaluated baselines, robustness to missing local observations, and further gains from autonomous retries.

title: Hetero-Associative Visuomotor Memory: Soft Recall as a Base for Learned Residuals in Few-Demonstration Imitation
summary: Retrieve-and-correct policies typically refine the nearest retrieved demonstration chunk, the readout that works best when executed directly. We study what a demonstration memory should supply to the corrector instead and find that a smooth, softmax-weighted recall over the whole memory is a much better base. On ALOHA cube transfer (40 human demonstrations), soft recall is no better to execute alone than the nearest chunk; however, with keys, candidates, and training fixed, correcting it raises success by 22.4 points on fresh resets with new encoders and by 7.4 against a closed-loop-tuned top-1 corrector. On robomimic Square, it leads by 7.9 points with the two better operators and by 6.7 on a label-free draw of equal size. This gain holds on sparse, varied demonstrations under an action-aware key and leave-one-demonstration-out training, and fades or slightly reverses on dense, scripted, or generated data. Building on this finding, our hetero-associative visuomotor memory (HAVM, 14M parameters) trains offline in about five minutes, including a learned retrieval temperature $\beta$, and runs in 1.1 ms. Across six fresh ALOHA encoders, it reaches 76.4% within 24 s, comparable to a 264M Diffusion Policy trained for 6.7 h (78.8%) and ahead of ACT (71.7%) and fine-tuned VLAs (65.2-75.2%), while leading every 40-demonstration baseline within the benchmark's 8 s limit (74.6%; +6.5 over Diffusion Policy, +15.1 over ACT). On LIBERO, one 40-task memory reaches 92.2% and loses far less than SmolVLA to rewording; on a real SO-101 arm, it sustains 30 Hz control without stalling. Unlike pretrained foundation policies aimed at zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks and workspaces, HAVM trades broad out-of-distribution generalization for rapid adaptation to the available demonstrations.

title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
summary: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. We propose 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision--language--action (VLA) framework integrating persistent visual referring (PVR), compressed temporal memory (CTM), and geometry-aligned trajectory supervision (GTS) for instance identification, motion reasoning, and three-dimensional control. Experiments across two VLA backbones show consistent gains over standard fine-tuning, with normalized average tracking frames increasing from 22.56\% to 35.28\% for $\pi_0$ and from 25.68\% to 33.64\% for $\pi_{0.5}$. Our benchmark further reveals a substantial gap between offline imitation accuracy and closed-loop tracking reliability, establishing a challenging testbed for future research this https URL

title: Normalizing Flows are Capable World Models
comment: An earlier version of this work was accepted at the Workshop on Learning Effective Abstractions for Planning (LEAP) at CoRL 2026
summary: A world model lets an agent anticipate the consequences of its actions and use imagined futures to make decisions. We introduce Normalizing-Flow World Model (NFWM), which pairs an invertible observation encoder with an action-conditioned probabilistic predictor. Because the encoder is invertible, the predicted distribution over latent states defines a distribution over future observations. Maximizing the exact conditional likelihood of those observations therefore trains the representation and dynamics jointly. An agent can plan directly in the learned latent space and decode sampled trajectories to inspect possible futures. On Teleport, these samples capture the two possible outcomes of the same action. In Flappy Bird, a world model trained by likelihood alone supports reward-based planning that reaches 100 pipes in all ten evaluated games. For goal-conditioned control, an auxiliary inverse-dynamics objective shapes the coordinates used to compare predicted states with a goal. On LIBERO, NFWM uses this distance to select successful action sequences more often than LeWM and SMWM. In Atari Boxing, training on imagined trajectories improves a policy beyond its behavior-cloned initialization. Together, these results establish normalizing flows as capable world models.

AI.tldr: NFWM 用可逆观测编码器加动作条件概率预测器构成世界模型，用未来观测的精确条件似然联合训练表征与动力学，并可直接在潜空间规划。作者报告：Teleport 上采样能区分同一动作的两种结果，Flappy Bird 上仅靠似然训练的世界模型在全部十局中达到 100 根管道。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出世界模型的作用是让智能体预判动作后果并用想象未来做决策，但未在摘要中明确说明现有方法的具体缺陷；因此本文的动机只能概括为：需要一个既能给出未来观测分布、又能让表征与动力学被同一目标联合训练的世界模型。
AI.method: 输入是观测与动作。方法把观测经可逆编码器映射到潜状态，再用动作条件概率预测器给出下一潜状态的分布；由于编码器可逆，潜状态上的分布等价于未来观测上的分布，于是可以直接最大化未来观测的精确条件似然，从而同时训练表征与动力学。输出是潜空间中的预测分布与可解码的采样轨迹：智能体在潜空间内直接规划，并把采样轨迹解码出来查看可能的未来。面向目标条件控制时，额外加入逆向动力学辅助目标，用来塑造比较预测状态与目标时所用的坐标；摘要未报告该辅助目标的具体形式与权重。
AI.result: 作者报告：Teleport 上采样轨迹能捕捉同一动作的两种可能结果；Flappy Bird 上仅用似然训练的世界模型支持基于奖励的规划，在全部十局评估中都达到 100 根管道；LIBERO 上 NFWM 用该距离比 LeWM 与 SMWM 更频繁地选出成功动作序列（摘要未给出数值）；Atari Boxing 上在想象轨迹上训练使策略优于其行为克隆初始化（摘要未给出数值）。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究而言，本文的核心主张是：可逆编码器使未来观测的精确条件似然成为可优化的训练目标，从而把表征学习与动作条件动力学统一起来，并支持在潜空间直接规划与解码想象未来；目标条件控制中可用逆向动力学辅助目标塑造状态比较的坐标。证据边界明确：摘要只给出 Teleport、Flappy Bird、LIBERO、Atari Boxing 上的定性或相对结果，未报告数值指标、真实机器人验证与效率数据，因此“normalizing flows 是合格的世界模型”这一结论应视为作者基于上述环境的论断，而非经独立验证的普适结论。

title: CamAct: Learning Robotic Manipulation from In-the-Wild Videos via Camera Motion
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models benefit from large, diverse datasets for robotic manipulation, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains costly. Recent work has explored egocentric videos as a source of supervision, primarily drawing on demonstrations of human-object interaction. We show that in-the-wild videos can improve robotic manipulation even when they contain no demonstrations of object manipulation. Specifically, camera motion recovered from these videos provides an additional source of motion supervision that complements robot demonstrations. Building on this finding, we introduce CamAct, which incorporates this camera-motion supervision into VLA policies alongside robot demonstrations, extending the use of human videos for manipulation learning beyond object interactions. Experiments show that incorporating this video supervision during fine-tuning improves success rates from 96.40% to 98.10% on LIBERO and from 22.96% to 29.32% on RoboCasa 365. The resulting policy also demonstrates strong results in out-of-distribution generalization on LIBERO-Plus and real-world manipulation tasks.

AI.tldr: CamAct 用"野外视频"中恢复的相机运动作为额外运动监督信号，与机器人示教一起微调 VLA 策略，使视频无需包含物体操作示教也能用于操作学习；作者报告 LIBERO 成功率 96.40%→98.10%、RoboCasa 365 22.96%→29.32%。
AI.motivation: VLA 模型需要大规模多样化的操作数据，但采集机器人示教成本高。已有工作把自我中心视频当作监督来源，但主要依赖"人物-物体交互"示教。本文要解决的问题是：当野外视频中根本不含物体操作示教时，这类视频是否仍可用于提升机器人操作。
AI.method: 输入是野外（in-the-wild）视频与机器人示教数据；方法先从这些视频中恢复相机运动，把它当作一种额外的运动监督信号，认为它能与机器人示教形成互补；再把该相机运动监督与机器人示教一起加入 VLA 策略的训练（摘要明确说是在 fine-tuning 阶段引入）。输出是一个可用于操作任务的 VLA 策略。相对基线的变化在于：监督信号从"仅机器人示教（以及此前的物体交互视频）"扩展到"不含物体操作示教的野外视频所提供的相机运动"。
AI.result: 作者报告，微调阶段加入该视频监督后，成功率在 LIBERO 上从 96.40% 提升到 98.10%，在 RoboCasa 365 上从 22.96% 提升到 29.32%；并称所得策略在 LIBERO-Plus 的分布外泛化与真实世界操作任务上也有良好表现（后者摘要未给出数值）。基线为未加入该视频监督的 VLA 微调设置（由前后对照隐含），摘要未报告数据集规模、硬件、试次数量与统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于：视频监督的价值可能不只来自"人手如何操作物体"这一语义内容，相机自身的运动也携带可迁移的运动信息，从而把可用的人类/野外视频范围扩大到无操作示教的视频。证据边界是：摘要只给出两个仿真基准上的成功率数值与对分布外泛化和真实任务的定性描述，未报告真实世界任务的量化结果、数据规模或消融，因此"相机运动是增益来源"这一因果解释尚属作者主张。

title: CARE-WM: Same-Horizon Self-Conditioning with Constraint-Adaptive Regularization for Latent World Models
summary: Planning with latent world models requires both accurate multi-step predictions and latent distances that reflect physical proximity to the goal. However, models are typically trained on ground-truth observations but must rely on their own imaginations during planning, while closer latent distances do not necessarily correspond to better task outcomes. Existing methods resort to auxiliary training objectives or additional task-cost readouts, which respectively incur extra training overhead or leave the latent geometry itself misaligned with task cost. We introduce CARE-WM, a drop-in training method that meets both requirements without additional supervision, a separate cost model, or any change to LeWM's architecture and Euclidean-cost planner. CARE-WM trains the predictor on its own predictions and adaptively calibrates the strength of latent regularization. With a single hyperparameter configuration, CARE-WM improves mean planning success over LeWM across all evaluated continuous-control tasks and matches or exceeds the best results of other LeWM-family methods on most tasks. Further analyses show lower open-loop latent prediction error and closer agreement between latent-cost rankings and physical task costs.

title: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics
summary: World models are increasingly used in robotics to improve the performance of embodied models. Compared with general-purpose video generation, robotics places more stringent requirements on world models. Generated videos must satisfy fine-grained physical constraints on robot motion and object interactions. However, existing world model benchmarks can overlook robotics specific physical details and struggle to assess them accurately. To address this problem, we introduce WorldPhy, a world model benchmark for accurate, fine-grained evaluation of physical plausibility in robotics. Our benchmark contains 300 tasks, each consisting of an initial-frame image and a task instruction, covering diverse robotics scenes, task categories, viewpoints, and robot configurations. We further collect over 12K high-quality human annotations, and use them to train WorldPhyReward to accurately provide scores and reasons across six fine-grained physical dimensions and an instruction-following dimension. Comparisons with general VLMs and existing reward models show that WorldPhyReward better aligns with human ratings. We system- atically evaluate 13 frontier open and closed-source world models. The results reveal that current world models struggle to consistently maintain fine-grained physical plausibility across different robotics scenarios. Our code is available at this https URL WorldPhy.

title: Escapingthe instruction blackhole of vision-language-action policies via optimal-transport wormholes
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are trained to follow a fixed instruction, yet people change their minds while the robot acts. We identify the instruction black hole: once a VLA policy commits to a task, new instructions are absorbed and the robot completes the old task or freezes. We quantify it with a transmission ratio and an event horizon and prove it is a blind spot of static imitation, which cannot distinguish a policy that listens from a deaf one once the execution state reveals the task. We propose Wormhole, a training-free plug-in that relocates the robot instead of re-instructing it: optimal transport selects an approach-phase state of the new task, a rate-limited traversal carries the robot there, and the unmodified policy takes over. On LIBERO,Wormhole raises committed-switch success of pi to and pi0.5 from at most 1.2% to 93.1%, matching or exceeding scripted retreat-and-restart with one fifth of its action discontinuity.

AI.tldr: VLA 策略一旦投入执行就会“吞掉”新指令（instruction black hole），作者提出无需训练的插件 Wormhole：用最优传输把机器人“搬运”到新任务的接近阶段状态，再由未修改的策略接管。在 LIBERO 上，π0 与 π0.5 的 committed-switch 成功率由至多 1.2% 提升到 93.1%。
AI.motivation: VLA 策略按固定指令训练，但人会在机器人执行中改变主意。作者指出存在“指令黑洞”：策略一旦承诺某个任务，新指令会被吸收，机器人要么把旧任务做完，要么冻结。作者用 transmission ratio 与 event horizon 量化该现象，并论证这是静态模仿的盲点——当执行状态已经暴露任务时，静态模仿无法区分“会听指令的策略”和“聋的策略”。
AI.method: 输入是执行中的机器人状态、原策略与一条新指令；方法不重新下指令，而是改变机器人所处状态。具体三步：用最优传输为新任务挑选一个接近阶段（approach-phase）状态；以受速率限制的遍历把机器人带到该状态；之后由未经修改的原策略继续接管完成任务。相对基线的变化在于：不做策略再训练、不做指令重写，只做“状态搬运”，因此是一个 training-free 的插件。

title: Ground Your Steps: Optimizing Sampling Schedules in Flow Matching Robot Policies
summary: Flow matching robot policies generate action chunks by integrating a learned velocity field at inference. However, under a fixed budget of neural function evaluations (NFEs), the integration result depends on the sampling schedule. This motivates optimizing the schedule to bring the generated action distribution closer to the demonstrations and improve task success. We propose Ground Your Steps (GYS), a training-free method that optimizes the sampling schedule by matching the generated and demonstrated chunk distributions at each observation. GYS applies truncated fractional differencing along each arm joint's action sequence and compares two types of pairwise differences between action chunks at each observation: differences of a generated chunk against a demonstration, and differences of two independent generated chunks against each other. After fractional differencing, these two pairwise-difference distributions coincide exactly when the distributions of generated and demonstrated action chunks match. GYS minimizes the energy distance between these distributions to obtain an improved schedule for each task and NFE budget. Compared with the uniform grid, GYS brings the generated chunk distribution closer to the demonstrated distribution and raises the success rate through the sampling schedule alone. On RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks, GYS improves success rates at nearly every budget, with gains of 2.8 percentage points for both $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7. The gains also transfer to three real-world manipulation tasks, reaching up to 3.3 percentage points. Code is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr:
固定神经函数评估次数（NFE）预算下，flow matching 机器人策略的积分结果取决于采样时刻表；GYS 提出无需训练的调度优化方法，使生成动作块分布更贴近示教分布。作者报告在 RoboTwin 2.0 上 π0.5 与 GR00T N1.7 成功率各提升 2.8 个百分点，三个真实世界操作任务最高提升 3.3 个百分点。</tldr>

title: $\widetilde{\varepsilon}$: Does Initial Noise Induce Directional Bias in Vision-Language-Action Models?
summary: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) have widely adopted diffusion-based action generation for continuous robot motions, enabling fine-grained control across diverse tasks. However, recent studies have shown that their performance is highly sensitive to initial noise, with resulting action errors that make recovery difficult during execution. Existing approaches search for favorable noise initializations to improve performance, yet the action expert itself remains sensitive to noise. In this work, we reveal that initial noise induces a consistent directional bias in action space that closely aligns with the noise's temporal mean. We thus introduce a simple yet effective framework that improves robustness to initial noise through interventions during both training and inference. During training, we enforce consistent action predictions from antithetic noise pairs $(\epsilon, -\epsilon)$ and, at inference, remove the noise's temporal mean. Our method substantially reduces action deviation and improves task performance across simulation benchmarks. In real-robot experiments, our method increases the average task success rate of $\pi_{0.5}$ from 40% to 68%, with more stable and consistent execution.

title: Rehearse in 3D, Render in 2D: Physically Consistent and Editable Robot World Models
summary: Embodied world models aim to predict future interactions that are both visually realistic and physically consistent. Yet explicit 3D motion prediction alone does not guarantee that object structure and contact relationships are preserved. Beyond motion prediction, 3D representations provide an explicit state space for imposing structural and physical constraints. Building on this insight, we introduce RehearsalWorld, an editable robot world model driven by 3D Interaction Rehearsal (3DIR). Given an initial RGB-D observation and robot actions, Interaction-Consistent Rehearsal (ICR) uses a pretrained 3D point-flow model as a motion prior. It refines the predicted trajectories through response-aware object grouping, persistent grasp memory, and contact structure refiner, preserving scene stability, object structure, and grasp attachments. Rehearsal-Aligned Video Generation (RAVG) then uses geometric projections of the rehearsal as temporal conditioning. We fine-tune a video generator on projection-video pairs to synthesize realistic interaction videos. Thanks to the decoupling of physical response from visual synthesis, RehearsalWorld also supports independent editing of material properties and camera viewpoints. Compared with PointWorld on real DROID grasping sequences, RehearsalWorld reduces gripper-relative offset by approximately 79% to 84% across deformable, articulated, and rigid objects and lowers reference motion error. For video prediction, it achieves a PSNR of 23.92 dB and an FVD of 149.

AI.tldr: RehearsalWorld 把机器人交互世界模型拆成"3D 排练 + 2D 渲染"两步：先在 3D 中生成物理一致的交互轨迹，再用其几何投影条件化视频生成器。作者报告在真实 DROID 抓取序列上相对 PointWorld 将夹爪相对偏移降低约 79%–84%，视频预测 PSNR 23.92 dB、FVD 149。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，具身世界模型需要预测既视觉真实又物理一致的未来交互；但仅做显式 3D 运动预测并不能保证物体结构与接触关系被保持。作者认为 3D 表示的价值不止于运动预测——它提供了一个可以显式施加结构与物理约束的状态空间。
AI.method: 输入是初始 RGB-D 观测与机器人动作。方法核心是 3D Interaction Rehearsal（3DIR）。第一步 Interaction-Consistent Rehearsal（ICR）：以预训练 3D point-flow 模型作为运动先验，再用 response-aware object grouping、persistent grasp memory 和 contact structure refiner 对预测轨迹进行细化，目标是保持场景稳定性、物体结构与抓取附着关系，产出 3D 的"排练"结果。第二步 Rehearsal-Aligned Video Generation（RAVG）：把排练结果的几何投影作为时间条件，在投影-视频对上微调视频生成器，合成真实感交互视频。相对既有"直接预测"路线的关键变化在于把物理响应与视觉合成解耦，因此材质属性与相机视角可以各自独立编辑。
AI.result: 作者报告两项结果：其一，在真实 DROID 抓取序列上，与 PointWorld 相比，RehearsalWorld 在可变形、关节式和刚性物体上把夹爪相对偏移降低约 79% 至 84%，并降低了参考运动误差（摘要以百分比表述降幅，未区分相对降幅与百分点）。其二，视频预测达到 PSNR 23.92 dB 与 FVD 149；摘要未报告该视频预测所用的数据集/基准与对比基线。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究而言，该工作提出了一种可编辑的世界模型结构：显式 3D 状态承担物理与结构约束，2D 生成网络只负责视觉真实感，从而在不重训物理逻辑的前提下切换材质与视角。证据边界在于：摘要只给出真实抓取序列上的相对偏移降幅与两项视频指标，未说明视频预测基准与基线、未报告消融、效率或部署情况，因此"物理一致性"的提升幅度与可编辑性的实际效果均无法由摘要独立验证。

title: DataForgeVLA: Fully Synthetic Manipulation Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Training
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Dataset available at this https URL
summary: We present a dataset of 340 fully synthetic manipulation demonstrations generated from real seed data for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) training. The corpus contains 32,340 frames with synchronized RGB and actions across eight object categories, represented as LeRobot v2.1 episodes with H.264 video, per-frame robot states and pose-valued action labels, language task annotations, summary statistics and quality decisions. Each synthetic demonstration is produced without additional teleoperation: a LoRA-fine-tuned Cosmos-3 model generates a manipulation video, and RoboHaMeR recovers the corresponding robot trajectory from RGB. Quality screening accepted 300 of 340 episodes for policy fine-tuning. As preliminary evidence of feasibility, a pretrained GR00T N1.6 policy fine-tuned exclusively on the 300 accepted episodes reaches 16/20 (80%) real-world pick-and-place success on the Oreo-package task. A policy fine-tuned on 105 real teleoperated episodes achieved 18/20 (90%) under the same protocol. These results are based on one object and 20 trials per policy and are therefore reported as preliminary evidence rather than a general performance claim.

AI.tldr: 该工作提出 DataForgeVLA：用微调的 Cosmos-3 从真实种子数据生成操作视频，再用 RoboHaMeR 从 RGB 恢复机器人轨迹，从而无需额外遥操作即可批量产出 VLA 训练演示；作者称仅在 300 条合成演示上微调的策略在真实抓放任务上达到 16/20（80%），并明确标注为单物体、20 次试验的初步证据。

title: WAtcher: Watching Ahead for Safe Robotic Manipulation with Efficient World-Action Models
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: World-action models (WAMs) couple future imagination with action generation, but they execute every action chunk while ignoring the potential risk. To fill this gap, we present WAtcher, a safety-aware world-action framework in which the policy imagines the outcome of the candidate chunk before execution. For fast future preview, WAtcher builds on a compact WAM whose video expert imagines the visual outcome in only two denoising steps. In addition, we propose Safe-Guard, a lightweight module kept outside the WAM that scores each candidate chunk from its imagined outcome and triggers a bounded retreat when the risk is high. Safe-Guard is detachable and can be applied to other WAMs. To train Safe-Guard, we build an autonomous pipeline to collect hazard data from RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real robot. Specifically, the pipeline perturbs expert demonstrations and labels each candidate chunk from the physical events recorded when it is executed, such as contacts and losses of support. Using the ~25,000 labeled windows from this pipeline, Safe-Guard reaches 92.1% balanced accuracy on a blind set, and cuts hazardous closed-loop trials on training tasks from 27.0% to 10.8% without lowering task success. On a held-out 300-question benchmark, it scores 94.2%, against 72.5% and 63.3% for zero-shot GPT-6-Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. WAtcher also reaches 90.4% and 82.4% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ManiSkill3, on par with or above leading WAMs, and 74.0% on five real-world tasks with Safe-Guard on, against 59.5% for $\pi_{0.5}$. AI.motivation: 作者指出的缺口是：WAM 把未来想象与动作生成耦合起来，但会执行每一个动作块，忽略其中潜在的（安全）风险。

title: Beyond Natural-Language Instructions: Temporal Logic as a Task Language for VLA Models with Visual-Logical Fusion
summary: Robotic tasks combine object relations, logical dependencies, and temporal requirements, which robot planning and industrial control commonly specify in temporal logic (TL). We introduce TL-VLA, a vision--language--action framework that replaces natural-language task instructions with temporal logic, making this spatiotemporal structure explicit. A typed graph encoder and visual--logical fusion condition continuous actions on the task specification and the current observations. To prepare a general vision--language backbone for this interface, we develop TL-aware robot pretraining with separate semantic and structural readouts: a frozen language teacher aligns task semantics, the structural readout encodes TL syntax to support complex, long-horizon tasks, and autoregressive action prediction connects the graph representation to robot behavior. Downstream policies inherit the pretrained backbone and TL encoder and learn new fusion and action modules. On CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, our TL-aware initializer reaches \textbf{3.800} average chain length and \textbf{62.3\%} five-task success, compared with 3.578 and 54.5\% for a FAST initializer pretrained on the same data and 3.485 average chain length for a Qwen+NL baseline. On LIBERO-10, TL-aware initialization improves success from \textbf{91.2\% to 95.8\%}. On LIBERO-Mem, our policy reaches \textbf{65.0\%} success without observation history, compared with 45.0\% for a Qwen+NL reference. On held-out Panda planning specifications, it reaches \textbf{59.6\%} at Success@256 over three generation seeds, versus 48.4\% for Qwen+TL and 37.0\% for Qwen+NL. These results support explicit logical task conditioning and transferable TL-aware representations for robot action learning.

title: Co-World Model for Human-Video-to-Robot Transfer via Co-Constructed Shared Latent Dynamics
summary: Human videos are abundant and cheap to obtain, whereas robot trajectories remain scarce and costly, making zero-shot skill transfer from a single human demonstration an appealing route to scalable robot learning. Existing methods, however, either retarget human-specific geometry or match only static visual goals, and thus stumble over the cross-embodiment dynamics mismatch and the ungrounded action execution. We present the Co-World Model (CoWM), a predictive framework jointly optimized from paired yet unsynchronized human and robot streams. To bridge the cross-embodiment dynamics gap, CoWM disentangles each observation into a shared object-relation state and embodiment-specific context. It aligns latent actions across embodiments using effect-swap and action-sensitivity objectives,such that actions are matched by their predicted effects on the manipulated objects rather than by embodimentdependent kinematics. For grounded execution, a phase-aware receding-horizon controller estimates demonstration progress, projects the inferred human action prior onto the robot action-support density, and translates the resulting latent dynamics into executable robot commands. Extensive experiments in simulation and on two physical robot platforms demonstrate the effectiveness of CoWM, its cross-platform generalizability, and the contribution of each component. See the demo video in the supporting information for details.

title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
summary: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. Inspired by human curiosity, we investigate how robots can formulate task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution. We propose CHASE, a Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence, which operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities. Four modules connect dynamic scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. The planner balances information value, skill reuse, and acquisition/execution cost. Missing skills trigger bounded exploration, learning from verified segments, and held-out admission during acquisition; separate checks verify physical effects and acquired evidence. Newly admitted skills expand the executable investigation set, closing the loop between resolving uncertainty and acquiring capabilities. Simulation and real-robot experiments evaluate investigation, skill acquisition, and task execution. CHASE achieves 50-80% task success under combined information and capability gaps, with 70-90% evidence resolution.

title: DriftWAM: Faster World-Action Models via Action-Aware Video Drifting
summary: World-action models (WAMs) unify future video prediction and action generation for robotic control, but their reliance on iterative denoising incurs substantial inference costs. Distilling these models into few-step generators offers a promising route to efficient deployment, yet maintaining task performance under aggressive step reduction remains challenging. Existing methods rely on point-wise trajectory consistency distillation, which pursues high visual fidelity while leaving downstream action information unexploited in optimizing video generation, and also lacks explicit distribution-level alignment. To address this, we propose DriftWAM, a few-step WAM distillation framework that incorporates the actions induced by predicted videos into video learning. Specifically, DriftWAM integrates action-aware video drifting, which performs video distribution matching through a joint visual--action similarity kernel to steer sample evolution under the guidance of these induced actions, with action-guided video regularization, which leverages the compatible teacher--student matches identified by the joint kernel to backpropagate action-level gradients directly into the video generator. Evaluations on the RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO benchmarks, as well as in real-world robotic manipulation tasks, show that DriftWAM consistently outperforms prior consistency distillation methods across few-step settings at the same inference speed.

AI.tldr: DriftWAM 针对 world-action models（WAMs）因迭代去噪导致推理成本高的问题，提出把动作信息纳入视频蒸馏的少步生成框架：用联合视觉–动作相似核做视频分布匹配，并把动作级梯度回传到视频生成器。作者称在 RoboTwin 2.0、LIBERO 及真实机器人操作任务上，相同推理速度下于多种少步设置中一致优于既有一致性蒸馏方法，但摘要未给出任何数值。
AI.motivation: WAM 把未来视频预测与动作生成统一起来用于机器人控制，但依赖迭代去噪，推理代价高。将其蒸馏为少步生成器是有前景的部署路径，然而在激进减少步数时保持任务性能仍然困难。摘要指出既有方法采用逐点（point-wise）轨迹一致性蒸馏，追求高视觉保真度，却在优化视频生成时未利用下游动作信息，也缺乏显式的分布级对齐。
AI.method: 输入是教师 WAM 的生成轨迹与由预测视频诱导出的动作。DriftWAM 做两件事：一是 action-aware video drifting，用联合视觉–动作相似核进行视频分布匹配，在诱导动作的引导下推动样本演化（分布级对齐，而非逐点轨迹对齐）；二是 action-guided video regularization，利用该联合核识别出的教师–学生匹配，把动作级梯度直接回传到视频生成器。输出是少步（few-step）的视频–动作生成器。相对基线（逐点轨迹一致性蒸馏）的改变在于：蒸馏目标从仅视觉保真度扩展为同时受动作信号与分布匹配约束。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究而言，该工作的要点是：少步蒸馏 WAM 时，把预测视频诱导的动作作为监督信号、并做分布级而非逐点对齐，可能比单纯追求视觉保真度更有利于下游控制。证据边界是摘要仅给出跨基准与真机任务的定性优越性陈述，缺少数值、步数配置、硬件与统计信息，无法判断加速倍数或性能保持程度。

title: Dynamic Task Update Benchmark (DTU-Bench): Evaluating Runtime Task Adaptation in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies perform well on fixed-instruction robotic manipulation benchmarks, but their ability to adapt to instruction changes during execution remains understudied. We introduce the Dynamic Task Update Benchmark (DTU-Bench), evaluating 40 task revisions across seven update types and three execution stages using LIBERO, a simulated robotic manipulation benchmark. We compare performance when a new instruction is given before execution starts versus during execution, and examine whether the new task instructions are followed. Across 13 representative VLA configurations, average task success is 95.8% on the original object-manipulation tasks, compared with only 1.6% when the instruction changes which object to manipulate during execution. Controlled diagnostics show that policies often complete the original task before the updated one, and that their responses depend on the robot's physical state. We further test whether a simple scripted controller that releases the grasped object and moves the arm back helps robots respond to instruction changes. This improves success from 2% to 38% for {\pi}0.5 and from 8% to 48% for DM0.5, but can cause unwanted object motion. These findings reveal limitations that fixed-instruction benchmarks and task-success metrics alone can overlook in evaluating robotic manipulation. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: VLA 策略在固定指令基准上表现良好,但执行中改指令时的适应能力缺乏评测。作者提出 DTU-Bench,在 LIBERO 仿真中以 40 个任务修订、7 类更新、3 个执行阶段检验 13 个 VLA 配置;当指令在执行中更换操作对象时,平均成功率从 95.8% 降至 1.6%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出,VLA 策略在"固定指令"的机器人操作基准上表现良好,但其在"执行过程中"适应指令变化的能力仍缺乏研究。这是该工作针对的具体空白。
AI.method: 输入是在 LIBERO(仿真机器人操作基准)中构造的指令更新场景:共 40 个任务修订,覆盖 7 种更新类型与 3 个执行阶段,并对比"执行开始前给出新指令"与"执行过程中给出新指令"两种时机。方法并不训练新策略,而是改变评测条件,并检查新任务指令是否被遵循;此外用受控诊断观察策略行为,并测试一个脚本化控制器(松开已抓取物体并把手臂移回)作为干预,看它能否帮助机器人响应指令变化。输出是指令更新的成功率、以及对策略行为与物理状态的诊断结论。

title: M$^{2}$AdaptVLA: Multimodal Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Model with Predictive Test-Time Adaptation
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures, 8 tables, including supplementary material
summary: Effective robotic manipulation calls for multimodal memory and rapid adaptation to shifts in contact dynamics. However, many existing policies, which retain either visual or wrench history, may miss key cues from the other modality. Moreover, even with wrench memory, fixed policies can struggle when contact conditions shift at deployment. To this end, we introduce M$^{2}$AdaptVLA, a vision-language-action model that integrates visual and wrench memories with predictive test-time adaptation. For visual memory, the model uses test-time training (TTT) to encode observation history in fast weights. Each entry in the bounded TTT bank combines the corresponding frame's features with a readout from these weights, preserving cues that predate the oldest retained frame. For wrench memory, a context gate controls how much the action expert draws on wrench history as it jointly denoises future actions and wrenches. For predictive test-time adaptation, the auxiliary wrench prediction loss also provides online self-supervision. Using measured wrenches as targets, we update low-rank policy adapters by backpropagating only through the final denoising step. Real-world experiments show that the TTT bank outperforms visual memory baselines on progress tracking, scene recall, and demonstration following. On contact-sensitive tasks, the context gate yields higher success rates than direct injection or gated cross-attention. Predictive test-time adaptation improves robustness to shifts in contact dynamics. On eight tasks requiring visual and wrench memory, M$^{2}$AdaptVLA achieves a mean success rate of 82.71%, a 31.46% absolute gain over the strongest baseline. The project page is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: M²AdaptVLA 把视觉历史与力/力矩（wrench）历史同时纳入 VLA 策略，并用预测式测试时自适应在线更新低秩适配器；作者在 8 个需要两种记忆的真实机器人任务上报告平均成功率 82.71%，相对最强基线绝对提升 31.46%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出的具体缺口有两个：现有策略通常只保留视觉历史或只保留 wrench 历史，会错过另一模态的关键线索；此外，即使有力觉记忆，当部署时接触动力学发生变化，固定策略仍会失效。
AI.method: 输入是观测历史（图像序列）与 wrench（力/力矩）历史，外加当前条件。视觉侧用测试时训练（TTT）把观测历史编码进 fast weights，并维护一个有界 TTT bank：每个条目把该帧特征与从这些权重读出的 readout 结合，从而保留比最旧保留帧更早的线索。wrench 侧是一个 context gate，控制动作专家在联合去噪未来动作与未来 wrench 时使用多少 wrench 历史。部署阶段做预测式测试时自适应：辅助的 wrench 预测损失充当在线自监督信号，以实测 wrench 为目标，只对最后一步去噪反传，用来更新低秩策略适配器。输出是去噪得到的动作（与 wrench）。相对基线，改变的是记忆的模态构成、wrench 的注入方式以及在线可更新性。
AI.result: 作者报告：真实机器人实验中 TTT bank 在 progress tracking、scene recall、demonstration following 上优于视觉记忆基线；在接触敏感任务上 context gate 成功率高于 direct injection 与 gated cross-attention；预测式测试时自适应提升了对接触动力学变化的鲁棒性。在 8 个需要视觉与 wrench 记忆的任务上，平均成功率 82.71%，相对最强基线为 31.46% 的绝对增益（摘要未给出该基线的具体数值，也未报告其他任务的逐项数字）。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于：把多模态历史（视觉 + 力觉）显式写入策略记忆，并把力觉预测当作部署时的自监督信号来在线校正低秩适配器，在摘要层面被作者报告为同时改善记忆类指标与接触敏感任务成功率。证据边界是：全部结论来自作者自述的真实机器人实验；摘要未报告硬件、试验次数、统计显著性与计算/时延开销，31.46% 为绝对增益而非相对百分比，具体基线未具名。

title: Compact Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environmentsvia On-Policy Training and Route-Bearing Output
summary: Instruction-following robots need navigation policies that reach high accuracy and remain inexpensive to train and to run on a single graphics processing unit (GPU). The most accurate vision-language navigation policies for continuous environments rely on language models with 4 to 8 billion parameters, long observation histories, and large auxiliary corpora. Two properties of the standard training setup limit smaller policies. Imitation labels cover the states that an expert visits, whereas the running policy reaches states that its own errors produce. In addition, an image-plane waypoint exists only while the route lies inside the camera view. We present \textbf{\paper}, a monocular red-green-blue (RGB) policy with 2 billion (2B) parameters that addresses both limitations. \paper adapts Qwen3-VL-2B with low-rank adapters and processes an eight-frame memory and the current view in one forward pass. The policy predicts the route direction as a bearing in the body frame of the agent, which remains defined for every heading, and a deterministic controller converts this bearing into motion. This design allows training to relabel the states that the policy itself visits. On-policy correction improves success, while bearing decoding outperforms image-plane waypoint scanning across all evaluated start headings with identical weights. On the \valunseen split, \paper achieves \rFinSR\% success on Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments (\rtor), averaged over three seeds, and \rRxFinSR\% on its Room-Across-Room counterpart (\rxr). Inference requires \rDecMs\,ms and \rInferGB\,GiB of memory, while training takes \rCostTrainTyp\ GPU-hours on one 12\,GB consumer GPU.
